t.meta_title: Claude Opus 5.5 — Research and Upgrade Plan
t.meta_desc: Research on Claude Opus 5.5 (released on 2026-09-22): pricing, benchmark charts, API changes and the upgrade plan for INEMA's systems.
t.hero_h1: Claude Opus 5.5: cheaper, stronger, with a new API
t.hero_lead: Pricing, benchmarks, what changes in the API and what to update in each system to use the new model.
t.hero_alt: Claude Opus 5.5 banner: research and upgrade plan
t.oque_h2: Cheaper than Opus 5 and ahead of it on almost everything
t.oque_sub: With four API changes that break older code. API ID claude-opus-5-5, 1M context, 128K output, default effort medium.
t.st3_d: approximate; Anthropic's estimate at default settings
t.oque_li1: Released on 2026-09-22, the first model of the "Claude 5.5" family. Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 arrive "in the coming weeks".
t.oque_li2: Available on claude.ai (Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise), Claude Code, the API, Bedrock (anthropic.claude-opus-5-5), Vertex, Foundry, Claude Platform on AWS and GitHub Copilot.
t.oque_li3: Official recommendation: "start with Opus 5.5 for most workloads". Fable 5.1 is for the most demanding reasoning.
t.oque_li4: Thinking is always on. The cost and latency lever is now effort, and the default dropped from high to medium.
t.oque_li5: Already in use on our server: in Claude Code 2.1.280 the opus alias resolves to claude-opus-5-5 (tested on 09/22). No system pins the new ID yet.
t.precos_sub: With the largest cache discount in the Opus line.
t.precos_src: US$ per million tokens. Source: Anthropic's official pricing page [PR]. Fast mode is a research preview, available only on the Claude API.
t.precos_note1: With cache reads at 0.05x of input, long agent sessions that re-read the same prefix (bots, Claude Code) get much cheaper. On the other hand, a cache miss weighs more in relative terms.
t.precos_note2: On subscriptions (Claude Code, claude.ai) per-token pricing is not visible, but Anthropic raised the 5-hour limits on paid plans.
t.bench_h2: Beats Opus 5 and Fable 5.1 on almost every system card test
t.bench_sub: And loses to GPT-6 Astra on three.
t.bench_n1: The official numbers are self-reported and measured at max effort (Terminal-Bench at xhigh), with production safeguards on. Several were run by partners (Cognition, Cursor, Zapier, Artificial Analysis).
t.bench_n2: Anthropic re-evaluates older models in every system card. Opus 5 scores 1861 on GDPval-AA v2 in its own card and 1708 on v2.1 in the 5.5 card. Do not mix tables.
t.bench_n3: Where Opus 5.5 loses: Terminal-Bench-Science (58.7 versus 64.6 for GPT-6 Astra), AutomationBench (40.0 versus 41.4), FrontierSWE v2 (62.3 versus 65.5) and OfficeQA (to Fable 5.1).
t.bench_n4: Not reported for 5.5: SWE-bench Verified, ARC-AGI, GPQA, AIME/USAMO, BrowseComp and τ-bench. The model does not appear on LMArena yet.
t.bench_n5: Anthropic itself says that "benchmark margins have become a less reliable guide" and that the real gap to Fable 5.1 "is smaller than the scores suggest".
t.effort_h2: At high, Opus 5.5 already beats Fable 5.1 at max
t.effort_sub: For less than a quarter of the cost per task, according to Artificial Analysis.
t.effort_li1: The default is now medium. If you don't set effort, you drop one level compared with Opus 5. In Anthropic's tests, 5.5 at medium beats Opus 5 at high on coding and knowledge work.
t.effort_li2: More effort does not always pay off. On FrontierCode, medium scores 54.6% and max 54.4%. On CursorBench, going from medium (52.5%, ~US$ 3 per task) to max (57.8%) gains about 5 points at a higher cost per task.
t.effort_li3: At the same level, it thinks more per turn than Opus 5, especially at xhigh and max. Leave headroom in max_tokens (64K is the suggested starting point for long agent turns).
t.api_h2: Four breaking changes and one silent change
t.api_sub: Compared with Opus 5. Anyone coming from 4.x also inherits the earlier restrictions.
t.api_r1a: Thinking cannot be turned off. {type:"disabled"} and budget_tokens are rejected at every effort level.
t.api_r1c: Omit thinking (or use adaptive) and control it with output_config.effort. For low latency, low.
t.api_r2a: No forced tool use. tool_choice any/tool are rejected, including in Batches and count_tokens.
t.api_r2c: auto + strict: true + an instruction in the prompt, and check that the call happened. To extract JSON, structured outputs.
t.api_r3a: Preserved thinking. Thinking blocks are bound to the model and the conversation. Accounts created on or after 2026-08-31 get a 400 if the history is edited.
t.api_r3c: Append-only history. A system message mid-conversation instead of editing the system. Or the thinking-binding-controls beta with drop_block.
t.api_r4a: Computer use only through computer_toolset_20260801. computer_20251124 is rejected (API and Google Cloud).
t.api_r4c: Change the tool declaration and the agent loop (the action becomes the block's name, several per turn).
t.api_r5a: Text between tool calls now arrives as progress thinking blocks, empty under the default display.
t.api_code_c1: # Before: accepted on Opus 5, 400 on Opus 5.5
t.api_code_c2: # After: thinking always on, effort is the control
t.api_her1: temperature, top_p and top_k with non-default values return 400 since Opus 4.7.
t.api_her2: Assistant message prefill returns 400 since Opus 4.6.
t.api_her3: The tokenizer from 4.7 onward produces 1x to 1.35x more tokens than earlier models.
t.api_seg: The first Opus with cyber, bio and reasoning-extraction classifiers (reasoning_extraction). A refusal comes back as HTTP 200 with stop_reason: "refusal". The recommendation is to enable server-side fallback (fallbacks: "default"), knowing that the fallback model runs without the 5.5 thinking blocks. The system card cites no ASL level and lists caveats: the model follows more malicious instructions pasted by the user and accepts more authorization claims that cannot be verified.
t.sis_h2: Where Claude runs today in INEMA's systems
t.sis_sub: Read-only server inventory on 2026-09-22: model, how it is called, what to do and priority.
t.sis_note_t: Two findings that come before any model switch
t.sis_note1: There are two claude installs. ~/.local/bin/claude is 2.1.280 and /usr/bin/claude is 2.1.63, from an old global npm. The 17 yt-scheduler*.service units and two crons put /usr/bin first in PATH, so they run the old version, which defaults to claude-opus-4-6. Changing the model in config does not reach them.
t.sis_note2: openpcbotv2 uses Agent SDK 0.2.50, which ships an embedded CLI 2.1.50. Update the SDK first, then change the ID.
t.sis_yt_f: Fix the units' PATH (or update /usr/bin/claude) and pass --model opus explicitly.
t.sis_v2_f: Update the SDK, switch to claude-opus-5-5 in the agent.yaml files, keep effort explicit and add xhigh to the type.
t.sis_v3_f: Nothing on the model. Check that effort is explicit in the yaml (the 5.5 default is medium).
t.sis_v3t_f: If the premium tier moves to Opus 5.5, remove temperature. Fix the opus-5 price table (it says 15/75; the right value is 5/25).
t.sis_cv_f: Add Opus 5.5 to the list and stop sending temperature to Claude 4.7+ models.
t.sis_cron_f: Same PATH fix as the schedulers.
t.sis_ccv_f: Switch to claude-opus-5-5 when it is reactivated.
t.sis_mv_f: Product decision: test Opus 5.5, which beats Fable 5.1 on most system card tests and costs 60% less.
t.sis_ccb_f: Nothing now. Sonnet 5.5 arrives within weeks and the alias upgrades on its own.
t.sis_icc_f: Keep it. If it ever moves to Opus 5.5, read the response by type (it uses content[0].text today, which breaks with thinking).
t.sis_leg_f: Stopped legacy. Update only if it runs again.
t.sis_src: Not using Claude: inemanews, inemaeventos and the portal news feed (Groq), webmcp-readiness, inemacbot, agentehermes, dsh-orchestrator and cerebro-pro.
t.guia_h2: From what unblocks the most to fine-tuning
t.guia_sub: Five steps with real commands. Order matters: without step 1, model switches never reach the services running the old CLI.
t.g1_p: Find out which claude each service sees and make all of them use the current version.
t.g1_c2: # option A: update the old global npm
t.g1_c3: # option B: in the yt-scheduler*.service units, put ~/.local/bin first in PATH
t.g2_p: The opus alias follows the newest model. Prefer the alias over pinning an ID; pin only where reproducibility matters.
t.g3_t: Change the ID where it is pinned
t.g3_p: In openpcbotv2, update the Agent SDK first and then change the model in the agent.yaml files, keeping effort explicit.
t.g3_c1: # 1) current SDK (0.2.50 ships an embedded CLI 2.1.50)
t.g4_p: Before pointing to Claude 4.7 or newer, remove temperature, top_p and top_k from the request body. The Opus 5.5 slug on OpenRouter still needs checking.
t.g5_p: For any code that calls the API directly (Anthropic's migration guide).
t.ck2: Remove thinking disabled and budget_tokens. Size max_tokens for thinking + reply. Read blocks by type.
t.ck5: Append-only history (preserved thinking). Handle stop_reason: "refusal" and enable fallback.
t.ck6: Set effort explicitly and measure low/medium before going higher.
t.ck7: UIs that showed text between tool calls: display: "updates".
t.ck8: Re-measure cost and latency. Review prompts written for Opus 5 (verbosity, verification).
t.guia_note: This page is the research and the plan. Applying it to production systems is a separate step.

t.src_sub: Research done on 2026-09-22, launch day: Anthropic's official documentation, third-party coverage and a read-only local inventory. Each chart uses a single source table. Self-reported numbers are marked as such.
t.effp_h3: In practice: the same app at six levels
t.effp_sub: Third-party test (2026-09-24): the same /goal in Claude Code at every level, turning ~105 GB of event recordings into an explorable 3D conference. One run per level, the author’s visual judgment, and cost estimated at API prices.
t.effp_r_low: Works, but wrong branding and static videos
t.effp_r_max: 2× the cost of xhigh, with more bugs
t.effp_r_ultra: Spawned no workflows; behaved like xhigh
t.effp_after: The GPT-6 Astra experiment with the same design reached the same pattern: the top level was not the preferred one, and there the winner was medium. Charts, the eight patterns and the data limits are in Effort in practice.
t.effp_op: Running Opus 5.5 on medium is the best option for everyday work. Go up to high when you need more reasoning and keep xhigh for extreme cases. The same goes for GPT-6 Astra. max stays out. This is a recorded opinion, not a rule.
